title: A Sense of Shame
note: This is the quality by which those raised high by worth, courtesy and the like feel shame at acts unworthy of them. That is why it follows those chapters.

couplets.plain: Real shame is shrinking from an act. The rest is the shyness of good women with lovely foreheads.
couplets.pm: The shame of good people is shame at a low deed. The kinds that come from holding in mind, speech and body are beyond them, and belong to women of good family with lovely foreheads. He rejects the reading that covering the body is like the shame of common women, since shame is held to ruin them and they aren’t named here.

links.quote: Real shame is shrinking from an act
links.reason: Separates real shame, felt at an act, from the shyness of women.

couplets.plain: Food, clothing and the rest are no different for anyone alive. What marks out a person is a sense of shame.
couplets.pm: Food, clothing and the rest are common to all human lives. The rest means sleep, fear and desire. What sets good people apart is a sense of shame, not these. Some read “fear” in place of “the rest”.

links.quote: What marks out a person is a sense of shame
links.reason: Food, clothing and the rest are common to all. A sense of shame alone marks a person out.

couplets.plain: All life is bound to flesh. Worth is bound to the good called shame.
couplets.pm: Every living thing takes the body as its base and doesn’t leave it. In the same way worth takes the good quality called shame as its base and doesn’t leave it. As life gets no fruit except with a body, worth gets none except with shame.

links.quote: Worth is bound to the good called shame
links.reason: Worth is bound to shame, as life is to flesh.

links.quote: All life is bound to flesh

couplets.plain: Isn’t shame the ornament of the worthy? Without it, isn’t a proud walk a disease?
couplets.pm: A sense of shame is the ornament of the worthy. Without that ornament, their proud walk is a disease to those who see it. Shame is an ornament because it beautifies, and the walk is a disease because it is hard to bear.

links.quote: Without it, isn’t a proud walk a disease?
links.reason: Without shame, a proud walk is only a disease.

links.quote: shame the ornament of the worthy
links.reason: Hangs shame on the worthy as their ornament.

couplets.plain: The world calls those who are ashamed of others’ blame as well as their own the home of shame.
couplets.pm: Those who feel shame at blame falling on others just as at blame falling on themselves, treating it as their own, are called by the world the dwelling place of shame. Such people are great, so all those of high standing praise them.

links.quote: ashamed of others’ blame as well as their own
links.reason: Praises those who feel the same shame at another’s blame as at their own.

couplets.plain: The best of people won’t want the wide world unless they have shame as their fence.
couplets.pm: The best people take shame as their protection and don’t want the wide world instead. It is a fence because it keeps out blame and sin. If shame and the world conflict, they take shame and not the world, the road by which those enter. Some say they want the world only with that fence.

links.quote: won’t want the wide world unless they have shame as their fence
links.reason: Even the wide world isn’t wanted without the fence of shame.

couplets.plain: Those who live by shame will give up life for shame. They won’t give up shame for life.
couplets.pm: Those who know the worth of shame and keep to it, when shame and life conflict, will give up life so that shame isn’t harmed. They won’t give up shame so that life isn’t harmed. Shame stands above life.
couplets.sensitive: praises giving up one's life to escape disgrace

links.quote: They won’t give up shame for life

couplets.plain: If a man feels no shame at what would shame others, righteousness has reason to feel shame.
couplets.pm: If a man shamelessly does a blameworthy thing that would shame those who hear or see it, that shamelessness is a fault for which righteousness leaves him. Righteousness doesn’t stay near someone with no tie to shame.

links.quote: righteousness has reason to feel shame
links.reason: Someone unmoved where others feel shame gives righteousness itself reason to feel shame.

couplets.plain: Failing in your principles burns your family’s name. Shamelessness, once it stays, burns all your good.
couplets.pm: If a man’s conduct fails, that failure ruins one thing only, the standing of his birth. If shamelessness stays in him and never leaves, it ruins all his good, whatever comes from birth, learning, character, deeds and company. Losing shame is far worse than losing conduct.

links.quote: Shamelessness, once it stays, burns all your good
links.reason: Ranks lasting shamelessness above any lapse of principle: it burns all your good.

couplets.plain: Those with no shame inside them move like a wooden puppet, whose string fools you into thinking it is alive.
couplets.pm: People with no shame in their hearts move about as if alive, as a wooden puppet, moved by the strings of its frame, deceives you into thinking it has life. Their movement is a puppet’s and not the movement of life.
couplets.sensitive: Says people without shame are not really alive.

links.quote: fools you into thinking it is alive
